transcript.text: Alright, thanks everyone for being here at the Sunday check-in. Before I settle the hive plan for this spring, I want to hear from each of you. Is there anything I should know about — concerns, ideas, schedule issues, anything at all — that ought to shape how we handle the hive this season? Take your time, one at a time is fine.

transcript.text: I need to raise something important before you settle the plan. My neighbor has a severe bee allergy, so the hive really needs to be moved to the far east fence — at least 50 feet away from the patio — and protected by a screened barrier. I should have brought this up sooner, but I wanted to make sure you heard it before finalizing anything.

I haven't mentioned this until now, but it definitely needs to factor into the plan before we settle anything.

If we move them before the new queen is established, we risk the colony rejecting her or even absconding. commitments.detail: Put up the screened barrier right away as a temporary safety measure for Nia's neighbor while we wait for the new queen to be established.
Ravi will handle introducing the new queen by May 15th and monitor the colony's acceptance and laying status before scheduling the physical move.
Once the new queen is accepted and laying, relocate the hive to the far east fence, at least 50 feet from the patio, with the screened barrier in place.
No honey harvest before June 1st to allow the colony to rebuild after queen introduction.
Twelve jars of honey ready for delivery to the Willow Street Hospice fundraiser by August 20th, 2026.
